'''''Ledebouria socialis''''', the '''silver squill''',  '''wood hyacinth''', or '''leopard lily''', is a [[geophyte|geophytic]] species of [[bulbous]] [[perennial plant]] native to the [[Eastern Cape|Eastern Cape Province]] of South Africa.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://plantcaretoday.com/silver-squill.html | title=Silver Squill Care: All About Growing Ledebouria Socialis | date=14 February 2022 }}</ref> It was first described by [[John Gilbert Baker]] as ''Scilla socialis'' in 1870.<ref name="GRIN">{{GRIN|name=''Scilla socialis'' Baker|id=33350|accessdate=14 March 2010}}</ref> [[John Peter Jessop]] later revised the genus ''[[Scilla]]'' and split off several species, reclassifying ''Scilla socialis'' into the genus ''Ledebouria'' in 1970.<ref name="IPNI">{{IPNI|id=537325-1|accessdate=14 March 2010}}</ref> It is often cultivated and grows well with minimal care.<ref name="Zachos">Zachos, E. 2005. [https://books.google.com/books?id=n2BExzst4YYC&pg=PA221 ''Tempting Tropicals: 175 Irresistible Indoor Plants''.] Portland, Oregon: Timber Press. pp. 221–222.</ref>

== Etymology ==
''Ledebouria'' is named for [[Carl Friedrich von Ledebour]] (1785–1851),<ref name= "gledhill">Gledhill, David (2008). "The Names of Plants". Cambridge University Press. {{ISBN|9780521866453}} (hardback), {{ISBN|9780521685535}} (paperback).  pp 232, 355</ref>  a botanist who published, among other things, the first complete Russian flora.<ref name="bio">{{cite web |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/bibliography/6606#/summary |title=Flora Rossica |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=1842 |website=Biodiversity Library |publisher=Biodiversity Heritage Library |access-date=4 July 2018 |quote=}}</ref>

''Socialis'' means 'growing in pure stands', 'dominant', or 'growing in colonies'.<ref name= "gledhill"/>
